prompt.en: A volunteer wants to reduce RF pickup on a long audio lead before opening any equipment. Which proposed change would NOT help that coupling path?

text.en: Add several ferrite turns on the audio lead close to the affected input.
Reroute the audio lead away from the antenna and transmitter cables.
Replace a two metre lead with a twelve metre spare lead coiled behind the mixer.
Clean or replace an oxidized plug that may act like a non-linear junction.

explanation.en: A longer coiled lead usually gives RF more conductor to couple into the audio input. The other actions reduce pickup or remove a likely detection point.

prompt.en: Two strong site carriers are at 150.9 MHz and 154.2 MHz. A receiver is bothered at 157.5 MHz only when both carriers are active. Which conclusion uses the arithmetic and placement correctly?

text.en: 154.2 - 150.9 = 3.3 MHz, so the receiver audio volume control is the best first adjustment.
2 x 154.2 - 150.9 = 157.5 MHz, so test filtering or attenuation before the receiver input.
150.9 + 154.2 = 305.1 MHz, so any filter after the first mixer will prevent front-end overload.
2 x 150.9 - 154.2 = 147.6 MHz, so a transmitter low-pass filter on the receiver feed line is the matching cure.

explanation.en: The third-order product 2 x 154.2 - 150.9 lands at 157.5 MHz. Reducing strong off-channel energy before the receiver input tests the suspected non-linear path.

prompt.en: A maintenance note says local Morse key clicks should be fixed by replacing the power-supply filter capacitor because the clicks happen at the key. What is the error in that note?

text.en: A filter capacitor controls supply ripple; local click energy is tied to the making and breaking of the key circuit.
The note should focus on voltage sag, because local key clicks are mainly slow chirp from oscillator drift.
The note should focus on parasitic oscillation, because local key clicks are always a self-oscillation above or below the carrier.
The note should focus on sending speed, because slower dots and dashes remove make-and-break RF without circuit changes.

explanation.en: For the local key-click clue, the make-and-break action in the key circuit is the issue. A power-supply filter capacitor is a ripple-control part, not the direct cure for that clue.
